items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: J. C. Heard taking his place and doing such an admirable job and really making it so smooth and easy to work with. I was there. You know we had an influx of young drummers that came in - Kansas Fields.

ctx.x: sit and look and hear guys play and he already knew he was the epitome. He was such a flexible man, you see. He knew the peoples that I knew from living in Washington - he knew the Johnsons, he knew the peoples. That's the reason he could understand me. I knew the Chick Webbs and Sid Catletts and what have you, but to know these peoples and to have that background, you see. It was something different, Milt.

Just hold it for a second while I change tape because we got a couple drummers I think we're going to talk about. So you were talking about J. C. Heard and when he joined Cab's band when Cozy had left to go to CBS. John Hammond finally got some things going where they would use some black people -

Dave Dexter, John Hammond, Raymond Scott - we were at Rockefeller Center. You was playing the Strand Theatre. I came to the Strand Theatre; I said, "Cozy, you are going to play with Raymond Scott at CBS." He said, "I'm with Fess." I said, "You're going to have to leave." Shortly after that - you know sometimes when we get into California there'd be 3 or 4 bands and you look up and you've got Cab, Duke, and Basie, and all of us will be there together. When we get there you know good and well that Cozy and I were…
